teenKit.tldr: When you speak, your skull bone-conduction boosts low frequencies, making your voice sound deeper to you than it actually is. When you hear a recording, you lose that internal bass boost, which triggers instant psychological cringe.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that the reality you experience in your own head is literally a custom-filtered illusion fabricated by your biology, meaning no two humans ever experience the exact same sensory world.
keyTakeaways: Your voice sounds strange on recordings because microphones capture air conduction only, while your ears receive a mix of air and skull bone-conduction.
Bone-conduction acts like an internal subwoofer, pumping low-frequency vibrations straight through your jaw and skull bones directly into your inner ear.
Audio illusions like 'Yanny vs. Laurel' prove that our brains actively interpret and flip ambiguous spectral contrasts based on subtle neurological cues.

vocab.meaning: The physical process where sound waves travel directly through your skull bones to vibrate your inner ear.
Sound traveling through the outside air into your outer ear canal, which is what microphones actually pick up.
A subconscious psychological bias where humans naturally prefer things that remind them of themselves.
The shifting ratio of high and low frequencies in an audio signal that our brains use to parse speech sounds.

quiz.question: Why does your voice sound higher and thinner on a voice recording compared to when you speak out loud?
options: Microphones alter frequencies to make people sound worse.
Your skull bone-conduction adds a deep bass boost that only you can hear.
Digital audio compression strips out all human vocal tones.
Your vocal cords actually change shape when you listen to recordings.
quiz.explanation: Bone conduction vibrates your skull with low frequencies when you speak, giving your live voice a rich bass that microphones completely miss.

quiz.question: What is 'implicit egotism' in the context of vocal recordings?
options: The arrogant belief that your voice is better than everyone else's.
A psychological trick where people refuse to admit they sound bad.
The unconscious bias where people prefer audio of their own voice if they don't realize it's theirs.
Anxiety caused by speaking in public settings.
quiz.explanation: Blind studies show that when people don't recognize their own recorded voice, they actually rate it quite favorably due to implicit egotism.

quiz.question: What role does the inner ear play in how we perceive sound?
options: It acts as a passive funnel with no active processing.
It uses precise molecular hardware like prestin proteins to mechanically process vibrations.
It translates sound waves directly into visual images in the brain.
It completely blocks out bone-conduction frequencies.
quiz.explanation: Specialized inner ear hardware, including motor proteins like prestin, actively amplifies and converts physical vibrations into neural signals.
